Also, there are no real ethics concerns about genetically modifying yeast like there are with other more advanced (read: potentially cute) organisms.

There's no easy way to answer that question. The short answer is "maybe". Gene therapy can in some cases modify DNA in a living subject, but the entire approach is still regarded as highly experimental due to mixed results, even though it has existed for decades now. The biggest problem is that gene therapy isn't a single programmable magic pill. It's usually a custom designed virus (other methods for delivery exist) that attempts to invade and modify cells so that when they divide, the new cells carry the impacted elements.

Unfortunately there are any number of things which can cause this all to fail - not the least of which is an immune response to the virus.
